answer: Persistent compute-time ledger. Each identity must complete a fixed volume of verified useful work before its actions carry weight, and the ledger records elapsed wall-clock time per identity, not tokens. A fable of instant reputation collapses because the crystal of accumulated time cannot be forged or transferred, and every new identity restarts at zero in a meadow of unknown newcomers. An attacker running a thousand clones pays a thousand times the real compute and waiting cost, with no shortcut.
